whyCurrentEvidenceIsInsufficient: The primary expired-chat provider barrier proves that the primary child reached the refresh endpoint. PID overlap or launching a second child while it is held does not prove that the contender read the same grant as expired or entered the refresh arbitration path.
The contender has no provider barrier acknowledgement when correct serialization prevents a second request. Its absent provider request is therefore compatible with it running only after release.
The fake provider deterministically maps rotated to stale for each child. Child-local HTTP ledgers and identical effects provide no unique response ordering and cannot prove stale-response rejection.
Existing staleRefreshResponse and staleRefreshTokenRejected values are not-exercised. The current receipt correctly does not claim rejection.

minimalRequiredPublicCapability.owner: The real Hermes auth refresh/persistence owner reached through the existing public chat command, at the point it observes an expired credential and arbitrates refresh or reloads after serialization.
minimalRequiredPublicCapability.existingOutput: Add an optional refreshPathDisposition field to the existing HermesAuthConcurrencyObservationV1 in the canonical @toy/contracts source; expose it through the existing CLI probe result and CheckView. Do not add a command, endpoint, side channel, private mock, or new protocol.

minimumFields.expiredGrantObserved: Boolean set only by the real owner after it has read the seeded grant and found that grant expired.
minimumFields.sourceGeneration: The existing non-secret synthetic generation label read from that same grant.

minimalRequiredPublicCapability.privacy: Report only synthetic generation and disposition; never credential or refresh-token bytes. For this case, run the contender before auth-add creates another grant, so the seeded profile has one refreshable grant and sourceGeneration identifies the same row.

filesForLaterSourceAdmission: the pinned Hermes auth refresh/persistence owner source reached by the existing public chat path
boundedOwnerPlan.writtenInterface: An additive field on the existing auth concurrency result, populated at the real owner decision boundary and asserted by the existing refresh-first case. The patch may transport that owner-produced value through the current result; the fixture wrapper may not synthesize it from PID, actor, barrier state, or response absence.
boundedOwnerPlan.case: Extend only the existing refresh-first case. Keep the existing add-first and before/after-replace cases and all current crash-cut coverage. Do not add an acceptance ID or registry row.
sequence: Start the real expired-chat child against the single seeded primary grant and hold its existing fake-provider response at refresh-response-pending.

While that response is held, start a second real public chat child against the same profile. Require its owner-produced receipt to say expiredGrantObserved=true, sourceGeneration=rotated, and refreshPathDisposition=joined-in-flight or reloaded-after-serialization.

Require exactly one refresh request for that same grant in the combined provider ledger while the primary response is held. A second provider request is a duplicate-refresh failure; a missing owner receipt is unsupported, not a pass.

Release the primary response, then use fresh public auth-list and chat readbacks to confirm the accepted generation remains usable, the independent added grant survives its existing add path, and the independent root remains unchanged. Keep auth-add's token exchange distinct from primary-grant refresh accounting.
boundedOwnerPlan.staleResponseSemantics: On the serialized branch, no second response exists, so staleRefreshResponse remains not-exercised. Do not relabel rotated-to-stale as rejected. If a future source path actually receives a superseded response, it may report stale-response-discarded only after the real owner discards that response and the fresh readback confirms the newer stored generation.
falsification: No expiredGrantObserved owner receipt for the contender: the test did not prove it reached the required path.
Contender reports provider-requested or the same-grant ledger records a second refresh while the first is held: duplicate-rotation predicate fails.
Contender sourceGeneration differs from the held primary grant: this is not same-grant contention.
After release, a fresh process does not use the single accepted primary generation or the independently added grant is lost: lost-update predicate fails.
